stem: In which changeover method are the old and new systems run **at the same time**?

options.rationale: Correct: both systems process the same data.
The old system stops when the new one starts.
One part is introduced at a time.
One location tries the system first.

explanation: Parallel running keeps the old system going alongside the new one.

stem: What is the main **disadvantage** of direct changeover?

options.content: If the new system fails there is no old system to fall back on
options.rationale: Correct: it is the riskiest method.

options.content: Staff must do all of their work twice, once on each system, for several weeks
options.rationale: That is a disadvantage of parallel running.

options.content: It takes a long time to reach every branch
options.rationale: That applies to pilot implementation.

options.content: It is the most expensive changeover method
options.rationale: Direct changeover is the cheapest.

explanation: Direct changeover is quick and cheap but has no fallback if the new system fails.

stem: A supermarket installs its new till system in its Mutare branch only, then in the other branches once it works well. Which method is this?

options.rationale: Phased introduces one part of the system at a time everywhere.
Parallel runs old and new together.
Direct switches everything at once.
Correct: the whole system is tried in one location first.

explanation: Trying the whole system in one branch first is a pilot.

stem: Changing a payroll system because the government has introduced a new tax rate is an example of:

options.rationale: There was no error in the system.
This is not an improvement requested by users.
Correct: the system is adapted to a change in its environment.
This is a changeover method.

explanation: Adaptive maintenance responds to changes such as new laws, rates or hardware.

stem: A district hospital is replacing its patient medication records system. Which changeover method is **most** suitable?

options.rationale: Too risky where errors could harm patients.

options.content: A changeover with no testing to save time
options.rationale: Not a valid method.
Correct: the old system remains as a fallback and results can be compared.

options.content: Switching off both systems for a week
options.rationale: Patients would be put at risk.

explanation: Where data is critical, the safety of parallel running justifies its cost.
hints: Which method is safest when errors could be life-threatening?

options.content: The whole system is introduced in one branch first
options.rationale: That is a pilot.

options.content: The old and new systems run together for a month
options.rationale: That is parallel running.

options.content: The old system is switched off as the new one starts
options.rationale: That is direct changeover.

options.content: One module at a time is introduced across the whole organisation
options.rationale: Correct: e.g. stock first, then sales, then payroll.

explanation: Phased implementation introduces the new system part by part.
hints: One part everywhere, or everything in one place?

stem: During evaluation, a new system is mainly compared with:

options.rationale: Comparisons with competitors are not the main purpose.

options.content: The objectives and requirements set at the start
options.rationale: Correct: evaluation checks whether these were met.

options.content: The price of the hardware and software bought for the new system
options.rationale: Cost is only one part, compared with the feasibility predictions.

options.content: The number of lines of program code
options.rationale: Code length says nothing about meeting needs.

explanation: Evaluation judges the system against its original objectives and the requirements specification.
hints: What is the evaluation measured against?

stem: A small school with one office is adding fees, marks and library modules. Staff are already busy, and the budget is small. Which changeover is **best**?

options.content: Parallel: run all three modules alongside paper records
options.rationale: Double work would overload busy staff and cost more.

options.content: Phased: introduce one module each term
options.rationale: Correct: staff learn one part at a time with no double work.

options.content: Pilot: try the system in one branch first
options.rationale: There is only one office, so a pilot is not possible.

options.content: Direct: switch all three modules on the same day
options.rationale: Too much change at once for busy staff, with no fallback.

explanation: Separate modules, busy staff and a small budget suit a phased introduction.
hints: Consider cost, risk and the number of parts.

stem: Parallel running is the safest changeover method but also the most expensive.
explanation: True. The old system is a fallback, but staff must do all the work twice.

stem: Fixing a bug that makes the system crash when a date is left blank is perfective maintenance.
explanation: False. Fixing an error is corrective maintenance; perfective maintenance improves a system that already works.

stem: Match each type of maintenance to an example.

right.content: Adding a search box that users have asked for
Fixing a total that is calculated wrongly
Updating the system to run on a new operating system

explanation: Corrective: errors. Adaptive: changes in the environment. Perfective: improvements.

stem: Match each changeover method to an advantage.

right.content: Staff learn one part of the system at a time
Problems are found in one location before full roll-out
Quickest and cheapest; benefits are immediate
Results can be compared with the old system

explanation: Direct: cheap and fast. Parallel: comparison and fallback. Phased: one part at a time. Pilot: one location first.
hints: Each advantage belongs to one method.

payload.template: Transferring existing records into the files of the new system is called data {{blank:a}}. After the records are loaded they should be {{blank:b}} to make sure they were copied accurately.

explanation: Data conversion; the loaded data is verified against the originals.
hints: Moving old records into the new files.

stem: During 20 working days of parallel running, 6 clerks each work 2 hours of overtime a day at USD 3 an hour. What is the total overtime cost in USD?
Describe **four** activities carried out during the implementation stage.

points.description: Installing the hardware (and preparing the site)
Converting / loading existing data into the new system (and verifying it)
Training users / completing documentation / changing over from the old system

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The new computers and network are installed, the software is installed and configured, existing records are converted and loaded into the new files and checked, and users are trained before the changeover.

explanation: Implementation puts the tested system into use.
hints: What must happen before users can work on the new system?

stem: A help-desk system had the objective *fewer than 3 complaints a week*. In its first four weeks the complaints were 4, 2, 1, 1. Evaluate whether the objective was met and suggest what the analyst should do next.

points.description: Calculates or describes the average (2 a week) or notes that week 1 had 4
Judges: met on average / in later weeks, but not in the first week (improving trend)
Next step: investigate early complaints / gather user feedback / recommend improvements or extra training

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The average was 2 complaints a week, so the objective was met overall, and complaints fell after the first week (4). The analyst should find out what caused the early complaints, perhaps a lack of training, and keep monitoring.

explanation: The average is 2, below 3, but week 1 exceeded the target.
hints: Compare the measured value with the objective.

stem: Zambezi Building Society (fictional) has eight branches. It is replacing its savings accounts system. Customers' balances must never be wrong.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which method would allow the society to try the system in the Masvingo branch before the others?

options.rationale: Phased introduces modules one at a time.
Correct.
Direct switches over everywhere at once.
Parallel runs both systems together.

parts.explanation: A pilot tries the whole system in one location.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The manager suggests direct changeover in all branches. Explain **why** this is not suitable and recommend an alternative.

points.description: Direct has no fallback: if the system fails, balances could be lost or wrong
Balances must never be wrong, so risk must be low / customers would be affected in all eight branches
Recommends parallel running (or pilot then parallel) with a reason

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: If the new system failed after a direct changeover there would be no old system to fall back on, and wrong balances would affect customers in all eight branches. The society should use parallel running, at least in a pilot branch, so the new balances can be checked against the old system.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: After a year, three changes are made. Classify each.

left.content: Interest is calculated wrongly for accounts opened in a leap year
A new central bank rule requires an extra report
Customers can now view their balance on a phone

parts.explanation: Wrong calculation: corrective. New rule: adaptive. New feature: perfective.

hints: How many branches? How critical is the data?

stem: A Harare courier company's new tracking system had these objectives: (1) a parcel's location found in under 10 seconds; (2) fewer than 2 lost parcels a month; (3) every driver able to use the app without help. After three months: location found in 4 seconds; 3 parcels lost a month; 18 of 20 drivers use the app without help.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Decide whether each objective has been met.
parts.explanation: 4 s < 10 s: met. 3 is not fewer than 2: not met. 18 of 20 is not every driver: not met.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Recommend improvements for the objectives that were not met.

points.description: Objective 2: investigate why parcels are lost (e.g. add scanning at each hand-over / validation)
Objective 3: extra training / simpler app screens / help screens for the two drivers
Recommend further review / perfective maintenance with a reason

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: To reduce lost parcels, require drivers to scan each parcel at every hand-over so its last location is always known. Give the two drivers extra training and add help screens to the app. Review the system again after three months.

hints: Compare each measured result with its objective.
